text:
maria: seeing a weird gap when stitching logs -> traces for eu-west1 GPU provisioning spike. Kibana search for request_id shows entries in pods A/B but no traceid links. started at ~08:42 UTC.
ken: ack. is this the same window as the provisioning SLO alert?
tim: yes, we got a burst of P99 latency alerts around 08:40-08:45, multiple autoscaler retries.
maria: exact query I ran in Kibana: `request_id:"req-8f3c*" AND @timestamp:[2026-03-18T08:40:00 TO 2026-03-18T08:50:00]` returns logs but `trace.id` field is missing on many lines.
ken: that smells like the log enrichment sidecar failing to attach trace headers. can you paste a raw log line?
maria: sure: `2026-03-18T08:41:07Z pod/gpu-provisioner-5b8c INFO request_id=req-8f3c23 action=start host=eu-west1` (no trace.id present)
ryan: ops-bot shows a redeploy of `gpu-provisioner` at 08:39 due to image rollback. maybe sidecar init order got broken.
ops-bot: ticket #INC-4821 created for gpu-provisioner redeploy at 2026-03-18T08:39:12Z (auto).
ken: try this Loki query to see if logs had trace header upstream: ` {app=\"gpu-provisioner\"} |= \"request_id=req-8f3c\" | json | line_format \"${__line__}\"`
maria: running now... getting ~1200 lines, ~60% have `trace_id` present, ~40% missing. pattern looks like older pods missing enrichment.
tim: check prom: `sum(rate(app_enrichment_failures_total[5m])) by (pod)` — any spike?
tim: (typo) meant: tim: check prom: `sum(rate(app_enrichment_failures_total[5m])) by (pod)`
ryan: grafana panel shows a jump in enrichment_failures on pods `gpu-provisioner-5b8c` & `gpu-provisioner-5c9d` starting 08:38.
ken: could be a race during rolling update — sidecar container might crash-loop and logs from before restart lose trace header. we should narrow by pod UID.
maria: I filtered by pod UID: `pod:"gpu-provisioner-5b8c"` and found ~200 lines at 08:39-08:42 with missing trace.
ken: any correlation with network flakes? ENI rotation logs?
ymaria: I also searched VPC NAT logs, saw a handful of `conntrack` resets in the same minute from those node IPs.
tim: that would cause some downstream header propagation failures. if the sidecar uses an in-memory header cache, a reconnect might reset it.
ryan: quick mitigation: re-roll the sidecar image with a backoff on init so it waits for the main container readiness. low-risk bump.
maria: agree, but before rollout can we backfill traces? need to join logs and traces by request_id for the SLO postmortem.
ken: easiest is to export the subset from Loki to a gzipped file and join on request_id against Jaeger's search results for the same window. I can run the export.
ryan: command I used before: `loki-canary query --query '{app=\"gpu-provisioner\"} |= \"request_id=req-8f3c\"' --start 2026-03-18T08:38:00Z --end 2026-03-18T08:46:00Z --out /tmp/provisioner-req-8f3c.jsonl.gz`
maria: thanks. once we have that I can run a simple join: `jq -r ".request_id + \" \" + .trace_id" file | sort | join -t' ' -j 1 traces_by_reqid`
tim: also add a short-lived alert to catch enrichment failures > 5 for a pod in 5m so we don't miss future races.
ken: created PR to add alert: `enrichment_sidecar_failure_count > 5` with 5m window, severity=page. link: https://git.redwood/repo/ops/alerts/pull/241
ryan: rolling the sidecar now to `v1.3.2-fix-init` (canary first). will monitor enrichment_failures and trace attach rate.
maria: can you annotate the SLO dashboard and add a note on the incident? I'll assemble the backfill results and post to the postmortem doc.
ops-bot: deploy gpu-provisioner-sidecar v1.3.2-fix-init started at 2026-03-18T09:02:12Z by ryan.
ken: FYI, runbook step: if trace enrichment missing across >20% of lines, consider rolling back that release and run local sidecar tests: /runbooks/trace-enrichment.md
maria: got it. tagging @tim for SLO numbers and @ryan for the deploy follow-up.
tim: will update SLO dashboard and bump the incident severity in the follow-up if error budget burn > 0.3%.
ryan: can confirm canary shows trace_id attachment back to ~98% after the roll. monitoring for 15m. :thumbsup:
maria: thanks all. I'll upload the exported logs + join results to the incident folder and start a short incident writeup.
ken: nice catch, team. :clap:
